summary: Implements ADR-0145 (accepted by the maintainer 2026-11-25) for TM-10/V9: a shared scope with review: true holds every write of a writer that is not a reviewer in the durable outbox as awaiting_review until a reviewer approves it. Write paths traced: REST retain, gateway retain (async and sync) and automatic retention all go through MemoryService.submit -> memory_outbox.submit -> outbox_put(held=...); the in-memory enqueue path refuses a reviewed scope (loading already refuses review without outbox_enabled). outbox_claim selects only pending, delete_pending, processing and accepted, so a held row is never delivered. New routes (B1): POST /v1/skirnir/memory/review needs an authenticated client whose scope is in reviewer_scopes (listed reviewer with read on the scope, re-derived per request), else 403; approve/reject need the same for the row's bank, else 404 for everyone else including the writer, so held operations are not revealed; unknown tokens get 401 (the existing every-route identity test covers the new routes). Approval re-checks the writer with service.current(write=True) and the bank binding and turns a writer that lost its right into revoked; the worker's delivery check stays as a second gate. Store (B4): outbox_review runs under the outbox advisory lock with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and changes only a row still awaiting_review in the reviewer's bank; approval passes the delivery capacity check. Payload lifetime (TM-12): rejection, expiry and revocation set payload NULL at once; session deletion and curator deletion turn a never-sent held row into deleted with payload NULL; held text stays at most review_expire_days. Bound (TM-08): held rows are excluded from outbox_capacity and limited per writer and bank by review_max_held (429 for that writer only), so one writer cannot block other clients' writes. The review list applies the content filter with the reviewer's private_addresses flag and withholds by id. Logs and metrics carry reviewer, writer, scope and fixed outcomes, never content; /admin/context gets counts per scope only. SQLite migration 2 rebuilds the outbox table (copy, drop, rename, indexes, triggers; DROP's implicit delete fires no trigger, so outbox_totals stay exact); PostgreSQL migration 7 swaps the CHECK constraint. Tool tools/memory_review.py reads URL and token from the environment only, verifies TLS by default and refuses http to non-loopback hosts. Finding fixed before publication: a synchronous gateway retain of a held write would have held one of the bounded sync slots until sync_wait_s and then answered a misleading 504; it now answers 202 with state awaiting_review at once (tested). Direct backend access bypasses review as it bypasses every grant (TM-11, documented).

tests.evidence: 22 tests, 9 PostgreSQL ones skipped locally without a DSN: config parse/load rules (incl. unknown reviewer, reviewer without read, review without outbox); SQLite migration 2 keeps rows and counts and the CHECK still refuses unknown states; HTTP: held -> listed -> approved -> delivered, reviewer's own write direct, reject/expiry/replay never deliver and drop text, gateway async and sync and automatic retention held, writer withdraws, held survives store restart, tool lists/shows/approves; rejected cases: writer/other writer/other-scope reviewer get 404, non-reviewer list 403, unknown token 401, revoked writer never delivered, review_max_held gives 429 while another writer is admitted, tool refuses clear text, credentials in URL, missing settings and CA.

No real Hindsight or Hermes: the synthetic backend records deliveries.
The router container image runs the new self-test only in CI.
A reviewer's approval is judgement, not proof of truth; facts already in a bank before review was enabled stay until a curator deletes them.
